text: A woman’s arm touched the soul of a great sculptor two thousand years ago, so that he wrought an image of it for the Parthenon which moves us still as it clasps lovingly the timeworn marble of a headless trunk. Maggie’s was such an arm as that, and it had the warm tints of life. A mad impulse seized on Stephen; he darted toward the arm, and showered kisses on it, clasping the wrist. But the next moment Maggie snatched it from him, and glared at him like a wounded war-goddess, quivering with rage and humiliation. “How dare you?” She spoke in a deeply shaken, half-smothered voice.
